spec: Poison: at End of Phase deal damage equal to its value to the holder, then reduce the value by 1. Stacking additive. Source: the zombie's Rotting Bite applies poison 2 on hit.
expect: a unit with poison 3 takes 3 then 2 then 1 and the status is gone on turn 4

spec: Burn: same tick as poison (Resist-mitigated, ruled 2026-08-20) and halves all healing received while held. Codex-published (79 uses). Source: the Burning Zombie (unit.zombie-burning, 6-BESTIARY-SETTLED) -- onTakingDamage, deal 1 Burn to the attacker; mixed into the horde one per four. Also removes the zombie literal hardcoded in setup.ts roster construction. Declares changesBaseline.
expect: burn 3 deals 3/2/1; healing while burning is halved, rounded down
reason: 1-EFFECTS-SETTLED.md marks status.burn not yet shaped and says not to reference it. Built anyway. Removed 2026-08-14; restore from f7e2041 when Effects publishes it.

spec: Add forest, rocky, rocky-hills, water, obstacle to TERRAIN alongside OPEN and HILLS, and teach terrainOf() their glyphs (f r R w x) from MAP-01's legend. NO RULES YET — every new kind behaves exactly like open. This item is pure plumbing and must be provably behaviour-neutral.
expect: map.field loads its real 7-terrain layout instead of collapsing to open/hills, and all four original baselines are BYTE-IDENTICAL because no existing map contains a new glyph
note: PLUMBING — declared neutral: the five new kinds must appear in the log and must NOT change state. Baselines: all five moved, and the reason is LABEL-ONLY — map.loaded now carries a terrain census by id instead of a bare hills count, because a log holding raw integers cannot tell forest from water. Proven: rebuilding the old map.loaded payload from the new one reproduces fed687ad / 9f243cac / eaa096cb / 4c71eb68 exactly. map.field additionally moved because its terrain array now carries real values. terrain.obstacle is NOT probed: no authored map contains one yet, so it genuinely is not wired in — it arrives with terrain.passable, which must add one to a map.

spec: moveCostOf gains a case per kind. SWITCH, do not decide: forest 2, rocky 2, rocky-hills 2, water 3-or-impassable, obstacle impassable. map.json leaves moveCost null ON PURPOSE — these are design decisions. Put each in SWITCHES.md with a default and let a sweep answer.
expect: reachable() shrinks on map.field relative to terrain.kinds, and the shrink is larger for a move-4 unit than a move-5 unit
note: Costs are SWITCHES, recorded in SWITCHES.md: terrain.forest.moveCost, terrain.rocky.moveCost, terrain.water.passable. IMPASSABLE (999) is introduced but unused — terrain.passable is the item that uses it.

spec: An impassable hex cannot be entered: reachable() never returns it and pathTo() never routes through it. Obstacles are impassable. Water passability is a SWITCH. This is the first terrain that can make a hex unreachable, so it is also the first that can strand a unit.
expect: no path on map.field ever enters an obstacle hex across 200 battles, and no battle ends capped because a unit could not find a route
note: Adds map.thicket (MAP-01 rows 10-21, cols 0-11) because no existing map had an obstacle, so the rule was untestable. Also hardens deployment: it now refuses impassable hexes loudly instead of placing a unit inside a wall. | Probed NEUTRAL, and that is the assertion, not a dodge: for a WALL, zero interactions is the pass condition. terrain.obstacle must appear on the board (it does, 75x) and must never appear in a moved event. The stronger form of the same claim is in the test — 0 obstacle entries across 60 battles and 13645 moves, and 0 capped outcomes proving the wall does not strand the AI.

spec: Terrain grants stat modifiers through the EXISTING stat pipeline — rows in terrainMods(), not new stations. Forest +10 dodge +1 armor. Water -10 accuracy. Rocky-hills as hills. Values are SWITCHES; map.json leaves coverBonus and modifiers null on purpose.
expect: a unit standing in forest shows terrain.forest rows in its effective(dodge) ledger, and hit rate against it drops measurably in a paired sweep
note: Zero changes to stats.ts or pipeline.ts — one table in maps.ts and four readers. Values are SWITCHES (terrain.forest.cover, terrain.rocky.cover, terrain.water.penalty). Baselines: map.open/ridge/flanks/highlands are UNTOUCHED because they contain only open and hills, whose values did not change. Only map.field and map.thicket move.

spec: A standing unit exerts ZoC on its six adjacent hexes. A unit that ENTERS a hex inside an enemy ZoC stops there — it may enter, then its movement ends. Downed and dead units exert nothing. THE AI IS DELIBERATELY BLIND TO THIS (Angela, 2026-08-13): it keeps its current scoring, picks a destination as if ZoC did not exist, and gets stopped short. That is accepted, not a defect.
expect: a unit pathing past an adjacent zombie ends its move on the first hex inside that zombie's ZoC, and the log carries move.stopped naming the unit that stopped it
note: BECAUSE THE AI IS BLIND: reachable() still offers hexes the unit cannot actually reach, so units will routinely end up somewhere they did not choose. That MUST emit move.stopped. A unit ending somewhere unexplained with no log line is the exact silent-failure class the harness exists to catch.

spec: Leaving a hex inside an enemy's ZoC provokes one free attack from that enemy, resolved through performAttack with its cheapest melee attack, then settle. Once per enemy per activation. Costs the attacker nothing. AI remains blind — it will walk into these.
expect: a kiting ranger adjacent to a zombie takes a hit when it disengages, the log shows the attack with causeId movement.aoo, and the ranger's damage-taken share rises measurably in a paired sweep
note: HAZARD: this lands damage MID-MOVE, so settle can fire inside executeMove's per-step loop. A unit can die between two steps, and victory can trigger mid-activation. executeMove already breaks on lifeState !== standing; that guard is now load-bearing and needs its own test.

spec: PUBLISHED: 1-EFFECTS-SETTLED.md — pool. Heals equal to its value at End of Phase, then -1. Poison mirrored, so one number reads both directions. Halved while status.burn is present (burn not yet shaped — do not implement that clause).
expect: regen 3 on a damaged unit heals 3 then 2 then 1, capped at max HP

spec: Weakness: lowers damage DEALT by 1 per point (not the Strength/Precision stats), reduces by 1 at End of Phase. Source: a new Ghoul enemy attack 'Sapping Claw' applying weakness 2. Add the Ghoul as part of this item.
expect: a warrior with weakness 2 does axe damage minus 2; the stat itself is unchanged

spec: Stunned: the unit cannot act at all, reduces by 1 at End of Phase. Source: the Ghoul Brute's heavy attack applies stun 1 on hit.
expect: a stunned unit produces no move and no primary, and the log says why

spec: Protection: reduces incoming damage at station 550 AND is reduced by the damage it absorbs. Also loses 1 at End of Phase. Additive when granted again. Source: landed together with ability.warrior.rally, which grants it.
expect: protection 3 hit for 2 absorbs 2 and drops to 1; then End of Phase takes it to 0

spec: Skeleton Archer: enemy, ranged role, 6 HP, 0 armour, 0 resist, 70 accuracy, 2 strength, 3 precision, movement 3, shortbow reach 4 precision physical.
expect: appears, kites, shoots, dies; zombies still behave unchanged

spec: Ghoul Brute: enemy, melee role, 18 HP, 2 armour, 55 accuracy, 6 strength, movement 3, one heavy attack at Strength +2.
expect: a slow heavy enemy that survives multiple hero turns

spec: Rally: warrior class power, grants Protection 2 to every ally within 2 hexes, 1 stamina, cooldown 4. Requires status.protection.
expect: every ally inside the radius gains protection 2; nobody outside does

spec: Volley: ranger class power, two separate bow hits against the same target, each rolling to hit independently. 2 stamina, cooldown 3.
expect: two to-hit rolls and up to two damage events per use; armour applies per hit

spec: Defender mode: stays within 2 hexes of the nearest ally with less than half HP, attacks anything adjacent, never advances alone.
expect: a defender never ends further than 2 from its charge while that ally lives

spec: Support mode: holds at range, prefers using abilities on allies over attacking, retreats when threatened.
expect: exercises the support role, which is currently declared and unused

spec: NOT A DEFECT — Angela: the Mage/Ranger split is intentional. The Mage deals MAGIC damage and the Ranger PHYSICAL, which diverge sharply once enemies carry armor; and the Mage has Arcane Bolt and more to come, while the Ranger is essentially just its attack. Raw damage-per-swing is therefore the wrong yardstick. What is still worth measuring: the staff is only distinguishable from the bow against a target with armor > 0, and every enemy in the game today has armor 0. Add an armored enemy, then sweep staff vs bow against it.
expect: against an armored enemy the Mage out-damages the Ranger, and against an unarmored one it does not — the split is visible in the sweep, not just in the design
note: Open question that IS real: attack.mage.strike was used 0 times in 300 battles, the same dead-content shape as Massive Strike. The melee option on a ranged unit may never be worth taking.

spec: PUBLISHED: 1-EFFECTS-SETTLED.md — poison and regeneration are stripped by water at the occupant END OF ACTIVATION. The rung is specified; do not re-decide it.
expect: a poisoned unit that walks into water loses the status, and the log shows status.expired with causeId terrain.water
note: I queued this asking which rung. It was already answered in the published file.
generalizationExempt: The design names exactly one anti-status terrain (GD SS4: water is THE retreat tile). The mechanism is trait data -- stripsOnEnter/stripsOnActivationEnd rows on wet -- so a second stripping terrain is a data row costing zero engine code the day one is designed.
killSwitchExempt: terrain.water is not a registry row the CF_DISABLE_IDS seam can remove -- terrain is an enum plus trait tables. The tests assert strip data and live battle events directly; a future terrain-registry refactor brings terrain under the seam.

spec: GROUND-REQUIREMENTS.md §1.1 names it terrain.impassable. MAP-01's legend calls it Obstruction, glyph x. The engine uses terrain.obstacle. Two names for one thing — Angela picks, then it goes in GLOSSARY.md and the other is retired.
expect: one id, in the glossary, and no occurrence of the other anywhere
note: BRING TO ANGELA — a naming collision is hers, not a switch.

spec: The trigger layer per GAME-DESIGN.md 5: hooks (onAttack/onMiss/onHit/onDamage/onKill/onTakingDamage/onActivationEnd), selectors (self/target), effects (status.apply/status.remove/damage), integer percent chance, party-wide Magic scaling. Chance resolves as a number with stations; firing is a rung. Rolls in perform only.
expect: all six baselines byte-identical, because no unit carries a trigger yet
note: turnEnd renamed to onActivationEnd -- GAME-DESIGN 5 uses the banned Turn/Activation collision. Four Hell TCG anti-patterns designed out with a test each. | 2026-08-15: COMBAT-SEQUENCE.md had onAttack at step 6 (after Apply), where a miss could never reach it. Angela moved it to step 1. The code was already right and the DOCUMENT was wrong -- luck, not correctness, so the per-hit order is now asserted in test/trigger.test.ts.

expect: poison lands on roughly 20% of zombie hits that dealt damage, and the applies rider is deleted
note: status.poison is PUBLISHED in 1-EFFECTS-SETTLED.md -- the only one of the three rows that is.

spec: Zombie: a SECOND, independent 20% onDamage, apply status.weakness 1 to target.
expect: both zombie triggers roll independently -- roughly 4% of damaging hits apply both
note: WAITING ON ANGELA: status.weakness is fully defined in GAME-DESIGN 5 (-1 damage per point, reduces damage dealt not the stats) but is not published in any SETTLED file. Buildable the moment she says GAME-DESIGN counts.

spec: Mage: 100% onAttack -- every swing, hit or miss -- apply status.burn to target, value = ceil(partyMagicSum / 5). Angela: this is compensation for the Mage's lower hit chance, and is deliberately NOT the flaming-bow onHit case.
expect: burn applies on misses too, and rises to 2 when the party Magic sum reaches 6
note: BLOCKED BY ANGELA'S OWN FILE: 1-EFFECTS-SETTLED.md says status.burn 'is not yet shaped, so do not reference it from another session yet'. Built once already and removed. The party-wide sum is already implemented and tested.

spec: DMG.VS_TARGET at 275: damage modifiers that read the TARGET -- its type/tags and its statuses. NOT triggers: they change a number, so they are a station in the one damage pipeline (Law 1). The status half needs nothing new; the type half needs tags[] on unit defs, which is Bestiary's call.
expect: '+50% vs poisoned' appears as a row in the damage ledger and in the replay waterfall
note: Captured in neither GAME-DESIGN.md nor GAME-ARCHITECTURE.md -- see TRIGGER-NOTES.md 2.

spec: One targeting vocabulary shared by abilities and triggers: select (self/unit/area) x side (ally/enemy/any) x optional radius x requireTags. Angela 2026-08-15.
expect: all six baselines byte-identical; nothing targets anything differently until content uses it
note: Also adds tags[] on units (the MECHANISM only -- which units are undead is session 6's) and the Spirit stat with partySpiritSum. ANGELA TO CONFIRM: the actor counts as one of its own allies by default; excludeSelf expresses the other reading.

spec: An attack may contain N hits. Angela 2026-08-15: each hit resolves COMPLETELY -- damage, triggers, settle -- before the next begins. No retargeting. Remaining hits are cancelled the moment the target stops standing. Hit 2 is re-resolved from scratch, never a replay of hit 1's preview, because hit 1 can apply a status that hit 2's damage reads.
expect: Double Toss throws two daggers at one target; a kill on the first cancels the second; poison applied by hit 1 is visible to hit 2's resolution
note: Each hit needs its own ordinal in the to-hit key or both daggers share one roll -- the same correlation bug as two triggers on one hit.

spec: Abilities get the trigger effect vocabulary (status.apply / status.remove / status.reduce / damage / heal) plus the target.model targeting, instead of always being damage. Unblocks Heal Ally and Poison Knives.
expect: an ability can heal an ally, and an ability can grant its user a trigger

spec: Movement becomes a chosen action from a list, like attacks. Angela 2026-08-15: one movement option THEN one attack-or-power, both optional. Most units start with one movement option; more arrive with levels. Rogue Sprint is move +3 for 2 stamina.
expect: a unit with two movement options picks one, and the log names which

spec: Spirit, identical to Magic including the party-wide sum (GAME-DESIGN 5). Angela 2026-08-15.
expect: partySpiritSum totals the side; 6 + 2 x Spirit is 6 at Spirit 0 and 10 at Spirit 2
note: The four provisional units carry spirit 0 -- a stated absence, not an invented value.

spec: onActivationEnd is in HOOKS, validated, glossed and banned-alias documented, and fireTriggers(ctx,'onActivationEnd',...) appears nowhere in src/. Call it at the end of every activation, for the unit that acted, whatever it did.
expect: a unit carrying an onActivationEnd trigger fires it once per activation, including an activation where it neither moved nor acted

spec: UnitDef carries BOTH `attributes` and `tags` for what a unit is. Content fills `attributes` (zombie: ['undead']); every reader — target.ts requireTags, the planned VS_TARGET station — uses `tags`, and no UnitDef sets it. So "target undead" finds no zombies. Collapse to one field (Law 11).
expect: resolveTargets with requireTags:["undead"] returns the zombies

spec: ability.ts:resolvePowerDamage is a second damage pipeline: DECLARE -> SOURCE_STAT -> MITIGATION -> FLOOR, skipping SOURCE_STATUS, CRIT and PROTECTION. So Weakness would not reduce a power and Protection would not absorb one. Constitution Law 1: one damage function. PROVEN NEUTRAL at landing: no live status declares reducesOutgoing/IncomingDamage, so the unified pipeline is byte-identical in every control battle -- the refactor is pure. The stations become consequential the day weakness/protection land as content.
expect: a power aimed at a unit holding an absorbing status is reduced by it, and the ledger says so

spec: RULED, Angela 2026-08-15: 'You cannot use a ranged attack on something adjacent. You can use a ranged attack on something not adjacent at -20.' Matches GAME-DESIGN 4 ('-20 if YOU are adjacent to an enemy, ranged only' / 'Ranged cannot target an adjacent enemy at all. You may shoot past it at something distant, at -20'). The engine had it inside out: it charged -20 when the TARGET was at distance 1 (now illegal) and nothing for shooting past an adjacent enemy (the case the rule exists for). Legality moves to canAttack; the penalty reads the SHOOTER's surroundings.
expect: a bow on an adjacent enemy is illegal; the same shot at range costs 20 more accuracy when an enemy stands next to the shooter and nothing when none does

spec: canAttack refuses any attack whose target is not standing, so a downed hero cannot be attacked at all. GAME-DESIGN 9: enemies roll at +20 against the downed, and a hit only accelerates the bleed-out counter — it never kills.
expect: an enemy can attack a downed hero, at +20, and the hit reduces bleedOut rather than hp

spec: RULED, Angela 2026-08-15: 'Bleed Out counter should be five phases, but it only moves forward at the end of the hero phase.' Was 3, advancing at Start of Turn. Counter becomes 5 and the rung moves into the End of Hero Phase ladder — not Start of Turn, not the enemy phase.
expect: a downed hero is set to 5, the counter advances only inside an End of Hero Phase ladder, and death arrives on the fifth tick

spec: COMBAT-SEQUENCE Start of Turn rung 3 is a victory check. battle.ts runs only advanceBleedOuts, whose settle is guarded by if (downed.length) — so with nobody downed, Start of Turn checks nothing.
expect: a battle that becomes decided between phases ends at Start of Turn rather than mid-activation

spec: Outcome is heroClear | wipe | capped. COMBAT-SEQUENCE specifies five: objectiveMet and retreat are missing from the type. Blocked in practice on scenario objectives existing, but the enum should not silently disagree.
expect: the Outcome type matches the document, and an unreachable arm is marked as such

spec: COMBAT-SEQUENCE: the End of Phase ladder must be "an ordered list of named rungs supplied by config ... so reordering it is a sweep axis rather than a diff." battle.ts:41-59 is four straight-line calls, and battle.ts:40 docstring already claims it is the config version.
expect: reordering the ladder is a config value a sweep can vary, and the log names each rung

spec: ACC.TERRAIN (400) and DMG.TERRAIN (300) were retired when terrain moved into the stat pipeline. Both constants still sit in the station tables reading as unbuilt gaps. Comment them as retired or delete them, so the next session does not "fix" them.
expect: the station tables distinguish retired from not-yet-built

spec: status.poison is declared shape:'pool'; core/status.ts's own table says poison is a counter (a pool is spent when something consumes it — protection, shields). shape is documentation and never branches, which is why a wrong one sits there indefinitely.
expect: the declared shape matches the shape table

spec: AttackDef gains an optional `accuracy` modifier applied at ACC.SITUATIONAL (700), which is reserved and empty. This is the station every later accuracy modifier needs: the attack-of-opportunity -20, flight -30, a per-attack plus or minus.
expect: an attack declaring accuracy:-10 shows 10 less hit chance in preview and in resolution, with a SITUATIONAL ledger row

spec: On a crit the engine always applies the +50% arm. GAME-DESIGN 4: flip a coin — half the time +50% before mitigation, half the time roll evenly among six injuries, with normal damage still landing. Two cups (critBranch, critInjury) because the weights and the table tune independently; the crit-effect stream is declared and never drawn. Also needs the Crit and Grit stats: crit chance is 3 + gear/badges + (final Accuracy - 100)/4 - target Grit, and the Grit term does not exist.
expect: over many crits the branch splits about evenly and each of the six injuries appears; a high-Grit target is crit measurably less often

spec: GAME-DESIGN 5 lists onEnter and startOfBattle among the hooks; COMBAT-SEQUENCE fires onEnter at battle setup and again at every wave arrival. Neither hook exists. onWounded and onEquip are also in that list and are blocked on wound levels and gear respectively.
expect: a unit placed at setup fires onEnter once, and settle runs after

spec: RULED, Angela 2026-08-15: 'I don't think we're ever gonna use exclude self. Because it's already either including or excluding heroes or things by target, but I don't think self will ever be one of those.' Delete Targeting.excludeSelf. The actor is always one of its own allies; side and requireTags are the only two axes an effect discriminates on. Removes the last ANGELA TO CONFIRM in src/.
expect: the field is gone from the type and from eligible(); an area heal still reaches the caster at every radius
unreachable: A deletion, and of a field nothing reached: no content uses the targeting model yet, so no battle log can mention it. Neutrality is proven instead by the six control baselines being byte-identical.

expect: with CF_DISABLE_IDS unset every registry is byte-identical (baseline proves it); with it set, rows vanish and referencing content fails loudly

gauntlet: not passed — 1 flag(s) warned; 1 exemption(s) taken

spec: RULED, Angela 2026-08-20: Resist mitigates Burn and Poison per tick, never Bleed. Per-tick damage = max(0, value - Resist); the status value decays on its own clock regardless. Canonical verify table (5 poison vs 2 resist): take 3,2,1,0,0. Flag: tickMitigatedByResist on StatusDef; poison sets it, bleed never will.
expect: the 5-vs-2 walk holds; zero resist is byte-old-behaviour; regen ticks untouched
generalizationExempt: Only one damaging tick status exists as published content (poison). The second instance is burn, which 1-EFFECTS-SETTLED explicitly marks not-yet-shaped -- do not reference. The flag is data on StatusDef, so burn setting it WILL be the zero-engine-code second instance the day it publishes.

spec: RULED 2026-08-20: the testing lane. Content invented to exercise a mechanic under test carries the `test` id kind, lives in content/ beside real rows, is excluded from the published-source contract, and never ships. Renames trigger.warrior.second-wind to test.warrior.second-wind as the first citizen. Declares changesBaseline: the hashes cover the event log and every trigger firing names its id (Law 12), so a rename moves every hash while outcomes stay identical.
expect: the id appears in battles under its test.* name; content-check reports it in the TESTING lane, not INVENTED

Give rules a toggle the WITHOUT arm can flip (a cfg switch per rule item, declared on the backlog row), and teach effect-size.mts to use it. A tool chore, not a design question -- moved out of the questions inbox 2026-08-20.
